# Independence assumption

## Overview

Sometimes observations within a group share more in common with each other than with observations from other groups — violating the **independence** assumption.

-   Group membership can be modeled as a **random effect**
-   Today: compare fixed-effect approach vs. mixed-effects approach

## The tick dataset

A researcher studies blood-ingestion rate of ticks as a function of time spent on the host:

-   Multiple ticks per dog → **pseudoreplication**
-   Response: blood volume ingested (ml)
-   Predictor: hours since attachment
-   Grouping: dog ID

## Setup

```{webr}
rm(list = ls())
library(lme4)
library(stats)

url_remote <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/"
path_git   <- "MTourani/WILD541_F2025/refs/heads/main/"
load(url(paste0(url_remote, path_git, "ticks.RData")))
str(ticks)
```

## Explore tick data

```{webr}
dog_colors <- rainbow(length(levels(ticks$dog.id)))
names(dog_colors) <- levels(ticks$dog.id)

plot(volume ~ hours, ticks,
     col = dog_colors[ticks$dog.id],
     pch = 1, cex = 1.2, lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Hours spent feeding",
     ylab = "Blood volume ingested (ml)")
```

## Fixed effects model (naive)

```{webr}
my_lm <- stats::lm(volume ~ scale(hours) + factor(dog.id),
                   data = ticks)
summary(my_lm)
```

::: callout-warning
This uses many degrees of freedom on dog IDs — impractical with many groups or sparse data.
:::

# Mixed effects regression

## Random intercepts model: frequentist

```{webr}
my_lmer <- lme4::lmer(
  volume ~ scale(hours) + (1 | dog.id),
  data = ticks
)
summary(my_lmer)
```

## Plot with fixed-effect line

```{webr}
plot(volume ~ hours, ticks,
     col = dog_colors[ticks$dog.id],
     pch = 1, cex = 1.2, lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Hours spent feeding",
     ylab = "Blood volume ingested (ml)")
abline(lme4::fixef(my_lmer), lwd = 3)
```

## Random intercepts: Bayesian (nimble)

```{webr}
#| cache: true
library(nimble)
library(coda)

list_data <- list(
  volume  = as.numeric(ticks$volume),
  n       = nrow(ticks),
  dog.id  = as.numeric(ticks$dog.id),
  ndog    = length(unique(ticks$dog.id)),
  hours   = as.numeric(scale(ticks$hours))
)

model_1 <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:n) {
    volume[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], sd = sd)
    mu[i]     <- a[dog.id[i]] + b_hour * hours[i]
  }
  for (i in 1:ndog) {
    a[i] ~ dnorm(mean.a, sd = sd.dog)
  }
  mean.a ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  sd.dog ~ dunif(0, 20)
  b_hour ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  sd     ~ dunif(0, 100)
})

inits  <- list(mean.a = rnorm(1), b_hour = rnorm(1),
               sd = rlnorm(1),    sd.dog = rlnorm(1))
params <- c("mean.a", "b_hour", "sd", "sd.dog")
ni <- 4000; nb <- 2000; nc <- 4; nt <- 1

out <- nimbleMCMC(
  code = model_1, constants = list_data,
  inits = inits, monitors = params,
  nburnin = nb, niter = ni, thin = nt, nchains = nc,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE, summary = TRUE
)
out$summary$all.chains
```

## Traceplots

```{webr}
#| cache: true
coda::traceplot(out$samples)
```
